key_insight: GrimAge epigenetic age acceleration was the only DNA methylation age measure consistently associated with higher all-cause dementia risk; associations across other clocks and neurodegenerative diseases were limited or inconsistent.
clinical_relevance: Current evidence is insufficient to support DNA methylation clocks as neurodegenerative disease biomarkers; this paper does not address AI or cancer drug discovery.
method: Systematic search of six databases for studies linking DNA methylation age metrics to neurodegenerative diseases.
Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects meta-analyses with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment.
Review of Mendelian randomization evidence for causality.
evidence_signal: The review included 37 observational studies with 46,365 participants and seven Mendelian randomization studies; longitudinal meta-analysis linked each SD increase in GrimAge acceleration to higher dementia risk (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02–1.20).
watch_item: Associations do not establish causality, and disease-specific methylation clocks require development and independent validation.
paper_title: Biological age measured by DNA methylation clocks and neurodegenerative diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis
